stem:
The cumulative frequency distribution of marks obtained by 50 students is given below.

Marks less than 20: 6
Marks less than 40: 18
Marks less than 60: 35
Marks less than 80: 46
Marks less than 100: 50

How many students scored marks in the class interval 40-60?

per_option_rationale.rationale: Frequency for 40-60 = cumulative frequency up to 60 minus cumulative frequency up to 40 = 35 - 18 = 17.
Reading cumulative frequency up to 40 directly as the class frequency instead of taking the difference.
Using the cumulative frequency up to 60 as if it were the class frequency for 40-60.
Computing 46 - 35 = 11, the frequency for the next class (60-80), instead of 35 - 18 for 40-60.

explanation: To recover class frequency from a less-than cumulative frequency table, subtract consecutive cumulative values. For class 40-60: frequency = CF(up to 60) - CF(up to 40) = 35 - 18 = 17.

explanation_sections.punchline: Class frequency = CF at upper boundary - CF at lower boundary = 35 - 18 = 17.
explanation_sections.approach: Identify the model: convert less-than ogive values to class frequencies by differencing. Decisive move: locate the two bracketing cumulative values. CF(less than 60) = 35, CF(less than 40) = 18. Frequency = 35 - 18 = 17.
explanation_sections.lesson: Class frequency from cumulative distribution = difference of cumulative frequencies at consecutive boundaries; never read the cumulative value directly as the class frequency.
explanation_sections.timing: 20 seconds. One subtraction. Trap: option 3 (35) is the cumulative frequency at 60, not the class frequency.
